about:
Circle City Metalworks operates from the Irvington neighborhood on the east side of Indianapolis, Indiana. The shop was founded in 2020 and is run by Ryan Mullin, who writes the company's blog and refers to the business as "our little metal shop."

The company provides custom metal fabrication services including design, plasma cutting, welding, painting, and installation. Its portfolio spans custom handrails, tables, address signs, security products, and apartment-complex signage. A 2024 blog post notes the firm's largest project to date: fabricating and installing components for Southport High School in Perry Township.

Customers range from homeowners seeking one-off pieces to commercial contractors and educational institutions. Residential clients order handrails and decorative signs, while apartment complexes and schools commission larger structural and signage packages. The shop also markets a line of security-oriented metal products.

Circle City Metalworks positions itself on the promise "You dream it, we make it," emphasizing turnkey custom work from concept through installation. The team highlights its ability to scale from small decorative items to a high-school campus project as evidence of its flexibility.
